title: How William Harvey Measured the Heart's Output in Half an Hour and Overthrew Fourteen Centuries of Galen — Harvey's 1628 De Motu Cordis Half-Hour Mass-Balance Audit (1,800 × 7.5 mL = 13.5 L vs. 5-L Blood Volume), Ibn al-Nafis Pulmonary Transit, Malpighi Capillaries & Adolf Fick's O₂ Cardiac Output Law

teenKit.tldr: For 1,400 years, doctors thought the heart was a sponge or a furnace running on spiritual energy, completely missing that it is actually a mechanical pump. William Harvey shattered that myth in 1628 using simple math and a 30-minute mass-balance audit.
teenKit.whyItMatters: Without understanding that blood circulates in a closed loop driven by a pump, modern medicine—from open-heart surgery to treating high blood pressure—would be entirely impossible.
keyTakeaways: Galen's ancient medical monopoly dominated for centuries, convincing smart people that the heart sucked blood through invisible holes in the wall dividing its left and right sides.
William Harvey used pure arithmetic—multiplying heart rate by output per beat—to prove the heart pumps way more blood than the body could possibly manufacture or consume from food.
Discovery stacked upon discovery: Ibn al-Nafis mapped the lungs, Malpighi found the missing microscopic capillaries, and Adolf Fick later proved blood flow laws using oxygen.

vocab.meaning: A method of tracking inputs and outputs to see if a system's math actually makes physical sense.
When an entire culture or community of experts is so blinded by a shared belief that they fail to see an obvious physical reality staring them in the face.
The journey of blood from the right side of the heart, through the lungs to pick up oxygen, and back to the left side.
Tiny, microscopic blood vessels that connect arteries to veins, acting as the bridge where oxygen and nutrients actually leak into your tissues.

quiz.question: What was the main flaw in Galen's ancient theory of the heart?
options: He thought the heart was a static sponge and furnace instead of a dynamic mechanical pump.
He correctly guessed the entire circulatory system using an MRI.
He believed blood flowed backward from the toes to the brain.
He refused to ever look at a human or animal body.
quiz.explanation: Galen and his followers viewed the heart as a mixing bowl and furnace for spiritual energy rather than a closed-loop mechanical pump.

quiz.question: How did William Harvey mathematically wreck the old theory of blood consumption in 1628?
options: He weighed people before and after they ran marathons.
He calculated that the heart pumps vastly more blood in half an hour than the body's total volume or what food could possibly replace.
He used an electron microscope to count every red blood cell in the body.
He proved blood evaporated through the skin every few minutes.
quiz.explanation: Harvey's mass-balance audit showed that pumping 13.5 liters of blood in 30 minutes meant the body would have to create and destroy blood impossibly fast if Galen were right.

quiz.question: What crucial piece of the puzzle did Marcello Malpighi discover later on?
options: The exact weight of the human soul
Microscopic capillaries connecting arteries and veins, proving how blood crosses over
A chemical test for oxygen levels in the lungs
The layout of the heart's internal valves
quiz.explanation: Malpighi found the microscopic capillaries that Harvey's work implied must exist, finally proving how blood gets from arteries into veins.
